phases.title: Bind the listener to tenancy scope
phases.goal: Every listener path resolves an explicit Scope; delete groups[0] and the flat allowlist.
phases.why_priority: Tenancy is dormant: MemoryService.bind() has no production call site, so 28 isolation tests prove only that an unused module works.
evidence: zero/core/memory_service.py:44-46,55-57 unbound service skips every check
phases.schema_impact: Tenancy tables created at listener start; already defined in zero/tenancy.
phases.config_impact: listener.allowed_group_ids becomes a discovery seed, not a runtime allowlist. Keep reading it one release; mark deprecated.
phases.security_impact: This is the cross-group leakage boundary.
phases.migration_impact: On first start import each allowed_group_ids entry as an ACTIVE group so existing deployments keep working.
tasks: Resolve a Scope per inbound message from chat id
Bind MemoryService per request via service.bind(scope, registry)
Replace groups[0] with iteration over active groups
Make last_starter_at and last_interject_at per-group keys
Import allowed_group_ids as seed groups on first start
tests: two active groups, starter due in each, each receives only its own
per-group starter and interject cooldowns are independent
message for an unknown chat is refused, not silently served
grep guard: no groups[0] or bare group [0] index in scripts/
phases.acceptance: No groups[0] or bare group index in scripts/run_listener.py or run_panel.py, enforced by a guard test.
phases.rollback: Single revert; tenancy tables are additive and unread by legacy code.
phases.commit_strategy: One commit: guard test + scope resolution + per-group cooldowns.

phases.title: Extend scope to jobs, queues, outboxes, files and quotas
phases.goal: Every stateful row carries (installation_id, group_id) and every read has an ownership predicate.
phases.why_priority: Scoped memory with unscoped files still leaks across groups.
phases.schema_impact: Additive nullable columns plus a backfill assigning existing rows to the default installation.
phases.security_impact: Cross-group artifact reads and file path traversal.
phases.migration_impact: Backfill required; must be idempotent and reversible.
tasks: Add ownership columns
Add predicates to every read
Backfill existing rows
Scope workspace paths by installation and group
tests: two groups create same-named artifacts; neither reads the other's
quota consumed in group A leaves group B untouched
SQL walk test: every stateful read has an ownership predicate
phases.acceptance: Automated SQL walk over zero/storage.py finds no unscoped stateful read.
phases.rollback: Columns additive and nullable; revert restores prior queries.
phases.commit_strategy: One commit per subsystem: office db, office workspace, proactive, storage.

phases.title: Wire zero/providers into IndependentRouter
phases.goal: IndependentRouter delegates to ProviderRegistry; no direct HTTP in zero/router.py.
phases.why_priority: Two provider systems will diverge; per-group model assignment cannot land on the legacy one.
phases.config_impact: router.providers.* translates to ProviderProfile at load; legacy YAML shape preserved.
phases.security_impact: Moves credential handling behind symbolic references and redaction.
tasks: Translate legacy config to profiles at load
Delegate completion to the registry
Keep legacy path behind a flag for one phase, then delete
tests: existing router tests pass unchanged
legacy config shape produces the expected profiles
phases.acceptance: zero/router.py contains no direct HTTP call.
phases.rollback: Flag flip back to the legacy path.
phases.commit_strategy: Commit 1 translation layer; commit 2 delegation; commit 3 remove legacy path.

phases.title: Consolidate authentication and remove the weak-password path
phases.goal: One auth system, no accepted default credential, sessions durable across restart.
phases.why_priority: admin/Admin is an accepted credential and sessions live in a process dict, so a restart logs everyone out and a second process cannot share them.
evidence: zero/panel_store.py:121 allow_weak when username=='admin' and password=='Admin'
zero/panel_api.py:102 self.sessions is an in-process dict
phases.schema_impact: New panel_sessions table (id, user, csrf, created, expires, ip hash).
phases.security_impact: Removes a documented default credential; adds durable revocation and audit.
phases.migration_impact: Additive table; existing admins keep their scrypt hashes.
tasks: Delete the weak-password allowance
Persist sessions
Reduce to one documented auth mechanism
Add audit events
tests: bootstrap refuses a weak password
sessions survive a restart
revocation is immediate
guard test greps for literal password comparison
phases.acceptance: No string comparison against a literal password anywhere in zero/.
phases.commit_strategy: Commit 1 remove weak path + test; commit 2 durable sessions; commit 3 unify mechanisms.

phases.title: Cover vendored JavaScript in SBOM and notices
phases.goal: panel/three.module.min.js appears in the SBOM and third-party notices.
phases.why_priority: Shipping a vendored MIT library absent from the bill of materials is a licence-compliance defect and is cheap to fix now.
evidence: sbom is python-only, 36 components, contains no 'three'
tasks: Emit a component for each vendored asset carrying a licence file
Add the asset to the notices table
tests: SBOM contains a component for every panel asset with a licence header
notices list it
phases.acceptance: test_release_artifacts asserts JS assets are covered.

phases.title: TelegramAdapter contract and event normalization
phases.goal: One protocol both transports satisfy plus a NormalizedEvent carrying chat, thread, sender, reply, media and scope.
phases.why_priority: Writing three adapters without a shared contract produces three divergent shapes.
evidence: aiogram used only by run_panel.py management bot
phases.security_impact: Normalization is where untrusted platform input is labelled as data.
tasks: Define the protocol
Define NormalizedEvent
Build a recorded-fixture test transport
tests: normalization of group, private, mention, reply, command, media, document and forum-topic events
phases.acceptance: No adapter imports telethon or aiogram outside its own module.
phases.commit_strategy: Single commit: contract + events + test transport.

phases.title: Bot Mode inbound
tests: mocked Bot API transport; command parsing; media download bounds
phases.acceptance: Inbound events normalize identically to the User Session adapter.

phases.title: Bot Mode outbound
tests: correct thread on reply; send failures surface rather than being ignored
phases.acceptance: Every send returns a result the caller checks.

phases.title: Bot Mode health and permission diagnostics
tests: missing rights reported, not silently swallowed
phases.acceptance: Diagnostics name the exact missing permission.

phases.title: User Session onboarding (OTP, 2FA, flood wait)
phases.security_impact: Session material must never reach an API response, a log or the panel.
tests: send OTP, verify OTP, optional 2FA, invalid code, expired code, flood wait, session replace, local revoke
session string never appears in any response or log
phases.acceptance: A test asserts session material is absent from every surface.

phases.title: User Session inbound/outbound
tests: parity with Bot adapter on the normalized event set
phases.acceptance: Both adapters pass the same contract suite.

phases.title: Hybrid capability routing
tests: preferred transport per capability; declared fallback; independent health
phases.acceptance: Routing decisions are explicit and logged.

phases.title: Hybrid deduplication
tests: both transports see one update, exactly one response is sent
phases.acceptance: No duplicate reply under concurrent delivery.

phases.title: Forum topic routing
tests: two topics in one group; replies land in the originating topic
phases.acceptance: Thread id round-trips through normalization and delivery.

phases.title: Per-group provider assignment
tests: two groups with different profiles route to different providers
phases.acceptance: Groups reference a profile name, never a credential.

phases.title: Typed Admin API
phases.goal: Typed request/response models, group scoping, validation and redaction on every endpoint, plus the six missing surfaces.
tests: every endpoint rejects unauthenticated and cross-group access
no response contains a resolved secret
phases.acceptance: Every endpoint has a typed model and a scope check.
phases.commit_strategy: One commit per resource group; split across sessions if needed.

phases.title: WebSearchService with web_search/web_fetch split
phases.security_impact: SSRF, private-network rejection, redirect validation, DNS-rebinding pinning.
tests: private address rejected
redirect to private address rejected
validated address pinned to the connection
tracking parameters stripped
quota and permission enforced per group
phases.acceptance: web_search and web_fetch are separate entry points with separate permissions.

phases.title: Map remaining V1 tables
phases.goal: Extend the SourceTable registry to the 13 remaining V1 memory tables.
evidence: zero/memory_v3/migration.py:176,186 maps only long_term_memory and medium_term_memory
15 V1 memory tables exist in zero/storage.py
phases.policy: RAG/archive content must not become durable memory automatically; quarantine ambiguous scope or ownership.
tests: per table: RED first, rollback, resume, count reconciliation, quarantine coverage
phases.acceptance: Per-table source/target/reused/quarantined counts reconcile.

phases.title: Panel: Memory page
phases.note: Must not show raw private memory by default.

clean-install smoke
runs non-root
volume persists across restart
graceful shutdown

contrast

ordering_rules: listener scope enforcement precedes Telegram adapters
adapter contract precedes Bot, User Session and Hybrid
auth consolidation precedes the typed Admin API
typed Admin API precedes panel pages
provider wiring precedes per-group model assignment
WebSearchService precedes the panel Web Search page
CI executed precedes the release gate
migration verification precedes any production migration package
clean public tree precedes the publication package
